scams.name: Pickpocketing at Tourist Hotspots
scams.description: Pickpocketing is the most common crime affecting tourists in Avignon. Thieves work the crowds around the Palace of the Popes, Pont d’Avignon, Place de l’Horloge, and both train stations, often in teams where one person creates a distraction while the others lift wallets and phones. Incidents climb sharply during the Festival d’Avignon in July, when the population roughly doubles overnight.
scams.avoidance: Use a cross-body bag worn to the front with secure zippers, or a money belt worn discreetly under clothing. Never leave phones, wallets, or bags unattended. Be especially vigilant in crowds.
scams.location: Palace of the Popes, Place de l’Horloge, Pont d’Avignon, Avignon train stations, Les Halles market

scams.name: Petition Clipboard Scam
scams.description: Groups of scammers, often pretending to be deaf or representing charities, approach visitors asking ‘Do you speak English?’ followed by a request to sign a petition. The petition is typically in English (suspicious in France). While you hold the clipboard, an accomplice rifles through your pockets or bags. They may also demand a donation after signing.
scams.avoidance: Firmly say ‘non merci’ and walk away without engaging. Never hold a clipboard offered by strangers. Keep your hands free and bags secured when approached.
scams.location: Tourist areas around major monuments, Place de l’Horloge, near train stations

scams.name: Fake Police Officer Scam
scams.description: Fake officers approach tourists, flash bogus badges, and ask to inspect your passport and wallet to ‘check for counterfeit bills.’ While examining your wallet, they palm cash. Some operate under the invented title ‘Tourist Police’ to sound more official. Real French police never inspect tourists’ wallets on the street.
scams.avoidance: Real officers only ask to see ID, never the wallet itself. Ask to see their *carte de police* clearly, and offer to walk to the nearest *commissariat* together — genuine officers will agree; scammers won’t. Do not hand over your passport or wallet. Walk toward a busy public area and dial 17 if you feel unsafe.
scams.location: Tourist areas, train stations, near hotels

scams.name: Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: Unofficial taxi drivers work the Avignon TGV station and airport, offering rides at inflated rates. Even licensed taxis sometimes display the night tariff during daytime hours, claim the meter is broken, or take longer routes through town to pad the fare.
scams.avoidance: Only use official taxis from designated taxi stands. Check that the meter shows the correct daytime tariff. Look for the official taxi sign on the roof. Use ride-hailing apps when possible.
scams.location: Avignon TGV station, Avignon Centre station, Avignon airport

scams.name: Festival d’Avignon Crowd Scams
scams.description: Each July, the Festival d’Avignon swells the city by hundreds of thousands of visitors. The crowds watching street performances, queuing for shows, or pushing through packed streets create near-ideal conditions for pickpockets. Prices at street vendors also spike significantly during the festival weeks.
scams.avoidance: Be extra vigilant during the festival period (early to late July). Keep valuables in front cross-body bags or hidden money belts. Avoid carrying large amounts of cash. Be especially careful when watching street performances.
scams.location: Palace of the Popes courtyard, Place de l’Horloge, all festival venues throughout the historic center

scams.name: Restaurant Tourist Trap Overcharging
scams.description: Some restaurants employ deceptive pricing: giving tourists English menus with higher prices, not mentioning cheaper set menus, pushing expensive bottled water when tap water is free, adding unauthorized charges to bills, and switching to cheaper wines when premium glasses are ordered.
scams.avoidance: Always ask for the French menu or both versions to compare. Request ‘une carafe d’eau’ for free tap water. Check if service is included. Review your bill carefully before paying.
scams.location: Place de l’Horloge, restaurants facing Palace of the Popes, tourist areas

scams.name: Les Halles Market Upselling
scams.description: Avignon’s covered market Les Halles has developed a reputation for inflated prices compared to other Provence markets. Vendors may employ aggressive upselling, recommending expensive items and adding products you did not request. Prices can be 3-4 times higher than comparable markets for identical products.
scams.avoidance: Know approximate prices before shopping. Politely decline recommendations for additional items. Ask for prices before items are packaged. Visit other Provence markets for comparison.

scams.name: ATM Skimming and Card Fraud
scams.description: Criminals install card skimming devices on ATM machines to capture card details and PIN numbers. These devices blend seamlessly with normal ATM hardware. Scammers may also use fake card slot overlays that cause your card to get stuck, then offer ‘help’ while capturing your PIN.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks rather than standalone machines. Cover the keypad completely when entering your PIN. Before inserting your card, inspect the machine for anything that looks crooked, loose, or damaged. Never accept help from strangers.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs in tourist areas, train stations, remote locations

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet Scam
scams.description: Scammers approach tourists and quickly weave a string bracelet around your wrist while maintaining friendly chatter. Once secured, they aggressively demand payment (often 10-20 euros). If you refuse, they may create a scene or an accomplice may use the distraction to pickpocket you.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets or crossed when approached. Firmly say ‘non’ and walk away without engaging. Never extend your hand or arm to anyone offering ‘free’ gifts. If tied, walk away without paying.
scams.location: Near major monuments, tourist gathering points

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A scammer ‘finds’ a gold ring on the ground near you and offers it as your lost property or as a lucky gift. They then ask for a finder’s fee (5-20 euros). Accomplices may corroborate that the ring looks valuable. The ring is actually worthless brass.
scams.avoidance: Simply walk away without engaging. Do not accept anything being ‘found’ near you. Ignore claims about the ring’s value or religious obligations.
scams.location: Tourist walkways, gardens, along the Rhône river

scams.name: Train Station Luggage Theft
scams.description: Thieves board TGV and regional trains posing as passengers, wait for a distraction, and grab bags from the overhead racks before stepping off just as the doors close. At stations, they offer unsolicited help with luggage and disappear with the bag instead of carrying it. With up to 400 such incidents reported monthly on French rail, it is organized work, not opportunism.
scams.avoidance: Keep luggage in sight at all times — ideally at your feet, not in overhead racks. Keep small valuables in a bag on your lap. Use luggage locks or a cable to tether larger bags to the rack. Decline all offers of help from strangers. Be especially alert during station stops, when most thefts occur.
scams.location: Avignon TGV station, Avignon Centre station, on TGV and regional trains

scams.name: Vacation Rental Fraud
scams.description: Fake vacation rental scams have increased across Provence. Scammers create attractive listings offering apartments at attractive prices, then request deposits via wire transfer outside the official platform. Tourists arrive to find the property doesn’t exist or belongs to someone else.
scams.avoidance: Book only through official platforms like Airbnb or Vrbo. Never pay outside the platform or via wire transfer. Verify host profiles and reviews carefully. Be suspicious of prices that seem too good to be true.
scams.location: Online — affecting bookings throughout Avignon and Provence
